newsitem.title: UK: N.Irish police report mortar attack on patrol.
newsitem.headline: N.Irish police report mortar attack on patrol.

text.p: Police in Northern Ireland said they were investigating an attack against a patrol car near the town of Downpatrick on Saturday night.

They said there had been a small explosion near the police car, which had also damaged a civilian car. Sky news said the explosion came from a mortar bomb -- a common weapon of the Irish Republican Army, which has reinstated its guerrilla war against British rule of the province.
Ronnie Flanagan, chief constable of Northern Ireland's police, said on Thursday the IRA was specifically targeting his forces.
"We have had a series of attacks that are very real attempts to kill," he said. "If these attacks continue, my fear is that killing will be the inevitable result."

The IRA, which wants to end British rule of Northern Ireland and reunite the province with the Irish republic, ended a 17-month truce in February 1996 and has launched a wave of attacks in Northern Ireland since Christmas.

Security chiefs fear that the latest IRA campaign will force the guerrillas' ideological foes, Protestant Loyalists who want the province to stay British, to end their own ceasefire and return to revenge attacks against the Catholic community.
On Saturday Archbishop Sean Brady, head of Ireland's Roman Catholic church, urged the IRA to call a halt to its campaign.

"I call for intense prayer on the part of all our people that the ceasefire may be restored," said Brady, urging a political settlement to the 27-year Northern Ireland conflict in which 3,200 people have died.
Just hours before, police announced the discovery of a high-powered sniper rifle hidden in the stairwell of a block of flats in Catholic West Belfast, an IRA stronghold.
